title: Deploy cost triage & residency dialogue - AmberWave
summary: Introductory cost-oriented discovery focusing on per-token unit economics, batching and KV cache levers, residency/VPC constraints, and options between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Agreed to run a short pilot benchmark (10k-100k tokens/day) and Redwood to share pricing scenarios, security pack, and suggested batching/cache configs.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private residency and VPC needs
action_items: Maya - Share two hosted vs dedicated pricing scenario sheets by 2026-02-10
Ethan - Draft pilot benchmark plan with target prompts and load profile by 2026-02-12
Priya - Provide current traffic patterns and monthly token estimate (best guess) by 2026-02-11
next_steps: Redwood send pricing scenarios and security pack
Schedule pilot kickoff (30-45 min) for week of Feb 16
AmberWave to supply sample prompts and SLO targets
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-07 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (AmberWave Head of ML), Priya Shah (Infra Lead), Carlos Mendes (CTO)

Auto-summary: quick intake on cost levers, residency needs, and a pilot to measure per-token economics with batching and KV cache.

[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, i'm maya with redwood inference, ethan's our se and we'll lean on him for perf questions. quick check, is the time still good?
[00:08] Jordan: yep sounds good, thanks. I'm jordan, lead ML at amberwave. we run route optimization and an entity extraction pipeline that is pretty chatty.
[00:15] Priya: priya here, infra. mainly concerned about data residency and how the vpc/private options look. also curious about burst capacity during peak routing windows.
[00:23] Carlos: and cto carlos — i'll listen for cost numbers and any lock-in-ish constraints.
[00:28] Maya: great. goal for today is to understand your usage patterns and budget constraints, and then walk through the levers — batching, kv cache, model choice, and hosting modes — that affect per-token unit economics.
[00:40] Ethan (SE): i can cover batching math, caching behavior, and what we've seen in similar logistics customers.
[00:45] Jordan: quick context — we currently run a mix: smaller classifiers on prem, and some LLM ops on a few gpus in cloud. rough monthly tokens today maybe 20M tokens, with spikes up to 2x during route recalcs. target is to get to 200-300M tokens/month over 12 months if things go well.
[01:05] Maya: good, that's helpful. can you sketch typical seq lengths?
[01:10] Jordan: most calls are 60-300 tokens, average ~150. sometimes longer when we synthesize routing briefings ~800 tokens.
[01:18] Ethan: ok, so the batch size distribution and prefix reuse looks promising. prefix caching could cut generation tokens significantly on repeated context — especially for reranking and short instruction templates.
[01:30] Priya: residency — we need to keep PII off public hosted unless it's in a dedicated VPC with our key management. is that something redwood supports?
[01:39] Maya: yes, we have Private deployments with customer-controlled VPC options and KMS integrations. we can do SOC2 + SSO integrations. the hosted api is easier but for regulated payloads you'd likely want dedicated or private.
[01:50] Carlos: what is the delta on price between hosted and dedicated? ballpark numbers are fine.
[01:55] Maya: ballpark — depending on model family, hosted can be about 15-30% higher per token than a fully committed dedicated pool if you have steady, high throughput. but hosted has operational simplicity and shared autoscale so bursts are cheaper. dedicated is better for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at commit. private on-premels adds infra and ops premium — think additional fixed monthly platform fees plus per-token at similar to dedicated.
[02:18] Jordan: can you put that into examples? like per-1k token cost for a 7B-ish model?
[02:24] Ethan: yes, rough example today for a 7B open-ish model at our benchmarks: hosted generation paths might land around $0.12 per 1k tokens for our standard run (including small overhead for streaming and infra). dedicated reserved pool for high-util could be $0.08 per 1k tokens after commit, and private on-prem might be comparable to dedicated plus a $Xk/month platform fee for support and licensing. those numbers are illustrative — final depends on quantization, batching efficiency, and cache hit rates.
[02:52] Priya: that 33% delta matters. our finance wants unit predictability. how much does caching change that?
[02:59] Ethan: caching is huge. with a good prefix/KV cache and 40-50% cache hit on repeated templates, we've seen effective token cost drop 20-40% because you avoid regen of large prefixes. continuous batching also helps during high concurrency windows.
[03:15] Jordan: hmm — we do a lot of template-based prompts, so caching could be high. how does TTL and invalidation work?
[03:22] Ethan: short answer — redwood's runtime supports prefix caching with configurable TTL and per-customer namespaces. TTL can be seconds to hours; invalidation via API hooks. note: some clients call it 'k-v cash' in docs, haha — transcription will butcher that.
[03:35] Maya: (laughs) we'll send the cache docs.
[03:38] Carlos: latency — if we batch more aggressively to reduce cost, what's the latency impact? we need sub-150ms on some inference calls.
[03:47] Ethan: there are two knobs: batching and routing. micro-batching at 10-50ms windows can reduce cost with minimal p99 impact. larger batching windows (100-200ms) shift tail latency up noticeably. for sub-150ms SLOs, we'd keep batching light and rely more on prefix cache and model quantization. also dedicated pools with pinned kernels reduce variance.
[04:10] Jordan: model choices — do you support quantized variants?
[04:13] Ethan: yes, quantization (8-bit, 4-bit ops) is in our Optimize toolkit. for many workloads 4-bit int8-ish gives 1.8-2.5x throughput improvement; unit cost drops proportionally, but you should validate quality on your prompts.
[04:28] Priya: ok. for private deployment we need KMS/HSM and audit logs for compliance — is that part of the package?
[04:35] Maya: yes, Private includes KMS integration and audit logging. we can also arrange an on-prem package with air-gapped options but that adds lead time.
[04:43] Carlos: what about data retention and delete APIs — we can't keep raw PII logs forever.
[04:48] Maya: we support configurable retention and immediate purge APIs for customer-managed data. the hosted plan has retention defaults but enterprise contracts can change that.
[04:56] Jordan: pilot idea — we could run a 2-week pilot with 10-30k tokens/day representative load, test both hosted and a small dedicated pool, and measure token delta with caching metrics. is that feasible?
[05:08] Ethan: absolutely. suggested pilot steps — 1) AmberWave provide sample prompts and expected traffic profile, 2) Redwood spin up test hosted endpoints and a small dedicated slice, 3) run benchmarks capturing raw token counts, cache hit rates, latency p50/p95/p99, and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:25] Priya: we'll need an nda and security pack before sharing samples with PII.
[05:30] Maya: we'll attach our security pack and an nda template.
[05:33] Carlos: can you also show worst-case burn numbers? finance wants a ceiling if caching is worse than expected.
[05:39] Maya: yes we'll provide sensitivity analyses: conservative (0% cache hit), expected (25-50% cache hit), optimistic (75% hit). each will have hosted vs dedicated cost columns and a rough monthly forecast for their projected 200-300M tokens target.
[05:55] Jordan: quick nit — our routing system is bursty during 2 windows/day for 20-30 mins each, sometimes generating 5-8x baseline. how does redwood handle bursting?
[06:05] Ethan: hosted auto-burst to spare capacity; dedicated can be configured with burst credit options to handle peaks, or autoscale rules to add nodes with some spin-up time. we recommend a hybrid approach: keep critical low-latency routes on dedicated and fall back to hosted as a burst overflow. that gives reliability and cost control.
[06:23] Priya: is there an SLA for fallback? and how transparent will the routing be?
[06:27] Maya: SLA depends on contract: dedicated gets stricter SLOs; hosted has best-effort baseline SLA. routing decisions are policy-driven and we surface logs/traces in Redwood Console so you can audit which pool handled the request.
[06:40] Jordan: what about vendor lock? if we pin to redwood-specific rollout APIs, is migration hard?
[06:46] Ethan: we try to keep the API standard (REST/SDKs) and allow model pinning. migration costs mainly come from KV cache patterns and operator scripts. we can provide export hooks and migration playbooks.
[06:58] Maya: want to talk about success criteria for the pilot?
[07:02] Jordan: finance wants <$0.10 per 1k tokens in expected scenario, or at least a clear path to it with dedicated + 4-bit quantization and a 40% cache hit. ops want p95 latency <200ms and clear burst behavior. security wants SOC2 and KMS options.
[07:19] Maya: good concrete goals. we'll map those in the pricing sensitivity sheet.
[07:24] Priya: timeline — we want procurement signed within a month if pilot results look good.
[07:29] Maya: noted. any blockers?
[07:32] Carlos: one more — will you show model variant tradeoffs? we care about hallucination rates vs token cost.
[07:38] Ethan: yes, part of the pilot we'll run a small eval set and track quality metrics alongside cost. the Optimize toolkit will recommend quantization and model variants per workload.
[07:48] Jordan: ok, good.
[07:50] Maya: quick recap — action items and next steps: (1) Maya to send pricing scenarios + security pack + nda; (2) Ethan to send pilot plan and required telemetry list; (3) AmberWave to share sample prompts and monthly estimates; (4) schedule pilot kickoff week of Feb 16. is that correct?
[08:10] Priya: yes.
[08:12] Carlos: yep.
[08:14] Jordan: fine by me.
[08:16] Maya: awesome. any other questions?
[08:18] Jordan: one micro-question — you mentioned KV cache namespace per customer, is there cost associated per namespace?
[08:24] Ethan: no separate namespace fee; cost is tied to the tokens saved and storage footprint if large. we'll show you expected savings in the pilot report.
[08:34] Priya: thanks.
[08:36] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack and a calendar invite.
[08:40] [meeting ends — casual chatter as people drop off]

Notes about transcript quality: occasional misheard tech terms (k-v cash vs kv cache), numeric estimates are illustrative.

End of transcript.
